Question #6
Which method is most commonly employed to ensure that subVIs execute in a well-defined order?
Wire the error in/out terminals of the subVIs to define their execution order
options: Add software timing to all subVIs and set the delay time
Place the subVIs in order on a block diagram from top to bottom
Add hardware timing to all subVIs and set the delay time
explanation: LabVIEW relies on dataflow, meaning a subVI cannot execute until it receives all required input data. Wiring the error in/out terminals creates a strict data dependency that forces the subVIs to execute sequentially.

The PROCESS.vi subVI represents a test that outputs one line of text each time the test runs.
When the calling VI stops, we need to have a log showing every line of data output from PROCESS.vi.
Which of the following VIs meets all these requirements in the most efficient manner?
explanation: Efficiency: Writing to the file exactly once outside the loop avoids the high disk I/O overhead of writing on every single iteration (which makes option A inefficient).Since the Write to Text File function only accepts a single string input (not an array of strings), using an auto-indexing tunnel (as seen in B and D) results in a broken wire, leaving C as the only valid and efficient solution that accumulates the data into a single string using a shift register.

Question #14
Boolean Master, Boolean 1, Boolean 2 and Boolean 3 are all set to TRUE before the VI runs.
The following actions are performed:
1. The VI is run.
2. After 1 second, Boolean Master is set to FALSE.
3. The stop button is clicked.
What are the values of Boolean 1, Boolean 2, and Boolean 3 after these actions are performed?
explanation: Boolean 1 is outside the While Loop, so it reads Boolean Master only once, when the VI starts. Since Master is initially TRUE, Boolean 1 remains TRUE. Boolean 2 is inside the While Loop, so it repeatedly reads Boolean Master. After 1 second, Master is changed to FALSE, so Boolean 2 becomes FALSE. Clicking Stop ends the loop. Boolean 3, which is after the loop, then executes and reads the current value of Master, which is FALSE.
